skill_drafts.description: Conditionally initialize and start a trace session at client startup if auto_start_session is enabled. Registers atexit handlers and creates trace context with configured tags and default settings.
skill_drafts.objective: Initialize tracing infrastructure on client startup
contraindications: Manual trace control is required by caller
Trace session already active and recording
workflow_steps: If not registered, call atexit.register(_end_init_trace_atexit) and set _atexit_registered = True
Verify _init_trace_context is None or span.is_recording() is False
Retrieve trace_name from config or use 'default'
Convert config.default_tags to list if present, else pass None
If trace context created successfully, instantiate Session(_init_trace_context)
Update global _client_init_trace_context and _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace for backward compatibility
triggers: Trace context is None or not currently recording
constraints: atexit handler must be registered only once (check _atexit_registered flag)
trace_name defaults to 'default' if not configured
default_tags must be converted to list if present
cautions: Ensure atexit handler is idempotent or guarded by flag to prevent duplicate registrations
Legacy global references must be updated atomically with trace context creation
If tracer.start_trace fails, trace context remains None and session is not created
output_contract: Trace context is created and actively recording; atexit handler is registered; legacy session reference is updated and accessible via global references for backward-compatible code paths.

metadata.prompt: Check if auto_start_session is enabled in config. If enabled and trace context is None or not recording, register an atexit handler, start a new trace with the configured trace_name (or 'default'), apply default_tags if present, and update legacy session references for backward compatibility.

skill_drafts.name: Register atexit cleanup handler
skill_drafts.description: Register a single atexit handler to ensure trace cleanup runs at process exit, guarding against duplicate registrations.

contraindications: Process cleanup not required or disabled

triggers: Client initialization; atexit handler not yet registered (_atexit_registered is False)
constraints: Must check flag before registration to prevent duplicates
Registration must occur exactly once per process
Callback function _end_init_trace_atexit must be defined and callable
cautions: Atexit handlers run in reverse registration order; ensure no circular dependencies with other handlers
Exceptions in the cleanup callback may prevent subsequent handlers from running
output_contract: _atexit_registered flag set to True; atexit.register() called exactly once with _end_init_trace_atexit callback; cleanup handler guaranteed to execute at process exit

metadata.prompt: Check if the atexit handler has already been registered using the _atexit_registered flag. This ensures the cleanup handler runs exactly once at process termination.

skill_drafts.name: Update legacy global references for backward compatibility
skill_drafts.description: Synchronize internal trace context and session objects to global module-level variables to maintain compatibility with legacy code paths using indirect access patterns.
skill_drafts.objective: Maintain backward compatibility with legacy session access patterns
applicable_signals: Legacy integration is active in the codebase
contraindications: Direct context passing is enforced throughout the codebase
Trace context creation failed or is None
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify trace context is not None and is recording', 'condition': 'self._init_trace_context is not None'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Verify legacy session object exists', 'condition': 'self._legacy_session_for_init_trace is not None'}
triggers: Legacy session object instantiated from trace context
Legacy code may access session via indirect module-level patterns
constraints: Must execute only after trace context and legacy session are successfully initialized
Global variables must be updated atomically to avoid inconsistent state
Update must occur before any legacy code path attempts to access the session
cautions: Global state mutation; ensure thread-safety if multi-threaded access is possible
Legacy code may cache references; updates may not be visible to already-initialized legacy modules
output_contract: Global variables _client_init_trace_context and _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace are updated to match instance state; legacy code paths can now access the current trace context via indirect module-level access.

metadata.prompt: After successfully creating a trace context and legacy session object, update the global module-level variables _client_init_trace_context and _client_legacy_session_for_init_trace to reference the newly created instance state. This ensures that legacy code accessing sessions via indirect patterns (e.g., agentops.legacy.get_session()) receives the current trace context without requiring refactoring.
